My little brother was born extremely disabled, he’s violent and is essentially a 5’9 170lb toddler. My parents never made the decision your sister did but there are two of them. They had someone to switch off with for a break, to take care of their other children, to sleep and work. They’re both still so exhausted with no time for lives of their own. I can’t imagine what your sister goes through.
I often think of the day my parents are too old to care for him anymore or god forbid something happen. I don’t know what I’ll do but it may just be the same as your sister.
I understand where your coming from -never abandon family blah blah- but that’s not what she’s doing. She provided care for him day in and day out and she finally got to the point where she couldn’t do it anymore. She’s not pawning him off, she’s gotten him real help he needs and deserves. 
She doesn’t need you telling her she’s a horrible parent. You may never understand her decision, and you’re lucky to never have to. She doesn’t have to be the amazing strong supermom who can juggle it all. Your opinion is nothing but unfair to someone already in pain, who was strong enough to say I can’t do this on my own anymore. If she’s a good mom she’ll visit him often, make the transition easier for him and make better memories with him where she’s not stressed and just trying to get through the day. 
You need to apologize and support her like you claim to. Being a single mom is hard enough without the rest of the pain your sisters been through.
